newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka stocks dip as local investors book profit.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka stocks dip as local investors book profit.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower for a second successive day on Monday as local investors booked profits, brokers said.

The all share index closed 10.1 points down at 855.7 with price declines outnumbering gains by 56 to 28. Blue chips John Keells Holdings fell 15 rupees to 370, National Development Bank 15 to 275 and Richard Pieris six to 146.
"Local investors, retail and some institutional, who bought before the interim results began coming out are booking profit," said Shanil Perera of Lanka Securitites.
"The local investors are taking profit, because they see many stocks near their full value," he added.
Colombo stocks, which rose over 70 points during July on good interim results up to June, began easing on profit-taking on Friday, brokers said.
Turnover on Monday was a low 60.4 million rupees.
Brokers said the downside of the index should be capped around 850 points, as they expect investors to return soon with profits.
"Buying should return soon. With the market the way it is and interest rates so low, equity investments continue to give the best return," said Prasanna Chandrasekera of John Keells Stock Brokers.
